title: BLAST: Balanced Sampling Time Series Corpus for Universal Forecasting Models

problem.claim: Universal forecasting models require diverse training data, but existing large-scale time series datasets contain biases and imbalanced distributions that can impair performance and generalization.

gap.claim: The role of data diversity in training universal time series forecasting models remains underexplored.

contributions.claim: BLAST is a pre-training corpus designed to enhance time series data diversity through balanced sampling.
BLAST incorporates 321 billion observations from publicly available datasets and characterizes time series patterns using statistical metrics.
BLAST uses grid-based implicit clustering, grid sampling, and grid mixup to provide balanced coverage of diverse patterns.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce BLAST as a novel pre-training corpus.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that models pre-trained on BLAST achieve state-of-the-art performance using fewer computational resources and training tokens than existing methods.
The authors report that data diversity improves training efficiency and model performance for universal forecasting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Universal forecasting has advanced zero-shot forecasting, while the importance of training-data diversity remains underexplored.
Existing large-scale datasets exhibit biases and imbalanced distributions.
BLAST is introduced as a balanced, diversity-oriented pre-training corpus.
The corpus combines large-scale observations, statistical characterization, grid partitioning, grid sampling, and grid mixup.
The authors report improved performance and efficiency for models pre-trained on BLAST.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that balanced coverage of diverse time series patterns supports strong forecasting performance with fewer resources and tokens.

interpretation.claim: Training-data composition may be a major determinant of both model quality and training efficiency.

application.claim: When constructing pre-training corpora, measure pattern diversity and address distributional imbalance through explicit sampling strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that balanced sampling improves every forecasting setting or dataset.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, statistical metrics, grid-partitioning details, or mixup procedure.
The abstract does not provide quantitative baselines, evaluation tasks, or experimental settings.
